A 32-year-old male with a history of IV drug use and methamphetamine-induced CTEPH presents to
the ED with worsening abdominal pain and fever. The pain began periumbilically and has progressed
to severe groin tenderness. Two weeks ago, he switched from rivaroxaban to warfarin due to insurance
issues. His vital signs show temperature 102.3°F, BP 95/60 mmHg (baseline low), pulse 91/min, and
respirations 28/min. Physical examination reveals bibasilar crackles, normal cardiac exam, and RLQ
tenderness with LLQ rebound tenderness. Laboratory findings include: Hemoglobin: 11 g/dL
Hematocrit: 35% WBC: 16,000/mm^3 (normal differential) Platelets: 190,000/mm^3 Na+: 137 mEq/L
Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 3.7 mEq/L HCO3-: 23 mEq/L BUN: 40 mg/dL Glucose: 110 mg/dL Creatinine: 0.8
mg/dL Ca2+: 9.1 mg/dL AST: 34 U/L ALT: 45 U/L INR: 6.2 PT: 40 seconds PTT: 70 seconds Blood
type: O positive Antibody screen: Negative The surgical team has confirmed the clinical diagnosis
without imaging. The next available OR time is in 5 hours. What is the most appropriate intervention for
surgical optimization? Answer Choices: (A) Recombinant factor VIIa (B) Fresh frozen plasma (C)
Aminocaproic acid (D) Vitamin K administration (E) Protamine (F) Platelet transfusion (G) Tranexamic
acid (H) Factor IX concentrate (I) Cryoprecipitate (J) Prothrombin complex concentrate
 A. Recombinant factor VIIa
B. Prothrombin complex concentrate
